newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dollar ends softer in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dollar ends softer in quiet trading.

text.p: * The Canadian dollar ended softer at C$1.3689 (US$0.7305) from Wednesday's open of C$1.3676 (US$0.7312) in light trade.

* Dealers said there was little trading interest in the Canadian dollar stronger than C$1.3700 (US$0.7299), while the U.S. dollar held gains against the mark and yen as Greenspan comments and EMU rumors emerged.

Traders said concern over the EMU timetable had sent the U.S. dollar into orbit against other major currencies, prompting fixed-income managers to consider increasing their weightings in non-European investments.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima on Wednesday reaffirmed the commitment of their countries to qualify for European economic and monetary union.
Waigel told reporters after the meeting in Bonn that the timetable was not as important as fulfilling the fiscal goals, while Klima said the treaty left room for interpretation.
"There is clearly a preference to own currencies where growth prospects are strong and to move away from currencies where growth prospects are pretty bleak," said Michael Rosenberg at Merrill Lynch.
U.S. Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan said at his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony this week that the U.S. economy was doing "exceptionally well."
As a result, Canada has weakened against the U.S. dollar, but strengthened on the crosses against the mark to 1.2510 from this morning's open of 1.2504 marks, but slid to 88.54 yen from 88.78 yen.
((Paul Casciato, Reuters Toronto Bureau 416 941-8100 or email: paul.casciato@reuters.com))
